blacklistabilityReview.evidence: USDD remains Upstream, not direct Yes. Current Pharos /api/stablecoins confirms Tron 73.7507094961% and Ethereum 25.0922994129%, both material, and BSC 1.1569566505% below 10% (Bittorrent dust is 0.0000344404%). The official deployment inventory identifies Tron TXDk8mbtRbXeYuMNS83CfKPaYYT8XWv9Hz, Ethereum 0x4f8e5de400de08b164e7421b3ee387f461becd1a and BSC 0x45e51bc23d592eb2dba86da3985299f7895d66ba. The prior verified-source review finds mint/rely/deny wards, ordinary holder transfers and allowance-gated burn, but no blacklist, holder freeze, seizure, pause or token upgrade path. The current exact-match Ethereum Sourcify source independently confirms that ward authority does not bypass holder allowance for burn or transfer; proxyResolution.isProxy=false. Current Tronscan identifies the canonical Tron token as verified non-proxy and its method map retains only the reviewed holder-transfer, allowance-burn and mint/ward methods. USDD's official freeze-free disclosure is consistent with, not a substitute for, these code findings. There is no declared parent. The 2026-08-10 review's historical 62.2% allocator plus 8.3% direct USDT =70.5% all-chain debt exposure remains historical, not a current reserve recertification. A new official API observation fetched 2026-10-19T06:17:38.420806Z measures $1,779,349,938.04 of all-chain vault debt, with SA001-A $814,431,711 on Tron plus $435,509,896 on Ethereum (BSC zero), totaling $1,249,941,607 or 70.2470930691%. Direct USDT PSM/vault debt adds $66,500,366.22 or 3.7373405196%. The global allocator discloses $509,922,380.7224389 USDT, $45,914,606.725523 USDT0, $1,031.962399 USDC and $724,556,815.6491401 USDS, totaling $1,280,394,835.059501; all destination chains/operators are included, with no unsupported attribution of global positions to Tron alone. USDT/USDT0/USDC terminate in issuer/custodian control. USDS is counted categorically because its shared Sky book independently exceeds 50% issuer/custodian exposure (the conservative DAI review floor is 50.8727210615%), not merely because DAO governance can upgrade USDS. Consequently the debt-weighted exposure is 73.9844335887%, strictly above 50%. TRX debt 25.7128092445% and sTRX debt 0.3027571668% remain in the denominator and do not count. Pro-rating USDS instead of categorical transitive counting gives a conservative 54.4554518301% debt exposure and still does not flip the primary verdict. Secondary gross-collateral sensitivity: official all-chain lockedValue totals $2,482,787,324.57; allocator debt plus direct USDT lockedValue gives 53.0271104178%. Replacing allocator lockedValue with its actual holdings gives a $2,513,240,552.629501 denominator and 53.5962863837% categorical exposure; pro-rating USDS at the conservative Sky floor instead gives 39.4330958559%. The gross sensitivity is not the primary debt-weighted test. The dated Tron-only reserve scaffold cannot be substituted for the all-chain primary denominator. APIs have no common block/checkpoint, so these are contemporaneous issuer disclosures, not fabricated pinned on-chain reserve totals.

branches.label: USDD governed CDP collateral types
branches.summary: Governed USDD collateral types share per-ilk Median, OSM, and Spot pricing followed by Dog and collateral-specific Clipper liquidation auctions.

feeds.path: Supported feeds -> per-collateral Median -> OSM current/next price -> Spot -> Vat

branches.fallbackBehavior: The OSM retains a current value and separately stages the next Median value; if updates stop, Vat continues using the last Spot value and the collateral price can become stale.

collateralParameters.note: Each collateral type has a governed Spot liquidation ratio and Dog liquidation capacity; USDD documentation states the minimum ratio varies by asset and illustrates a 130% liquidation threshold.

branches.liquidationMechanism: When a Vault falls below its collateral-specific minimum ratio, Dog initiates liquidation and the corresponding Clipper sells collateral through a descending-price Dutch auction; proceeds repay USDD debt and penalties and surplus collateral returns to the user.
branches.backstop: Collateral-auction proceeds cover Vault debt; the documented system architecture provides Vow accounting and a Flop debt-auction path that sells governance tokens to recapitalize a protocol deficit.
branches.shutdownOrBadDebtBehavior: Uncovered system deficits can proceed to the documented debt-auction path. Deployment records also identify End and ESM contracts on supported CDP chains for emergency shutdown and settlement.
